question.problem: In a right triangle $△XYZ,$ $∠X$ is a right angle, $XZ=\sqrt{5}$ and $YZ=7.$ Find the cosine of $∠Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224552/assets/ea0502e8b261358c7b55c60df02474c5b39a75cbb104d6ba3efb40300294ef56.png)

Recall the definition of cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡Y=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{XY}{YZ}=\frac{XY}{7}
$$

Here, we need to determine the missing side $XY.$ The trick is to use the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}XY & =\sqrt{Y{Z}^{2}-X{Z}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{7}^{2}-(\sqrt{5})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{49-5} \\  & =\sqrt{44} \\  & =2\sqrt{11}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡Y & =\frac{XY}{7}=\frac{2\sqrt{11}}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
